title: Contrastive quality scorer for quantized-profile calibration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a contrastive quality scorer service that computes per-quant-profile deltas against float32 baselines across a heterogeneous set of metrics (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE, QA F1, and semantic similarity). This scorer will power calibration workflows and automated gating for rollout decisions.

Scope:
- Metric implementations: normalized perplexity delta, multi-task accuracy for MMLU-like suites (top-k where applicable), BLEU and ROUGE variants with length-normalization, QA F1 for span extraction tasks, embedding cosine similarity and semantic-F1 for generative outputs.
- Aggregation: task-weighted composite score with configurable weights stored per-project.
- Contrastive output diff: per-output token / span diff summaries and example-level failure buckets (e.g., hallucination, truncation, token-substitution patterns).
- Integration points: calibration job runner (calibration pipeline writes per-profile metrics), rollout gating API (compare incoming profile to baseline thresholds), Console dashboard panel for profile drift and metric histograms.

Design notes:
- All metrics return both absolute and normalized deltas (delta and z-score relative to historical baseline). Perplexity produced as exponentiated cross-entropy but reported as log-perplexity to stabilize aggregation.
- For MMLU-style tasks, compute per-task accuracy and confusion matrices; include top-1, top-3 accuracy and a partial-credit scorer for closely-related choices.
- BLEU/ROUGE computed with sacreBLEU-compatible tokenization and sentence-level bootstrapped confidence intervals. For long-form summarization, add ROUGE-LCS and a length-penalty term to penalize extreme brevity.
- Semantic similarity measured via a standardized embedding model (configurable) and reported as mean cosine and P99 tail. Also implement a QA-based semantic-F1 for generated answers vs. references using an NLU model to extract comparable spans.
- Composite score formula (initial): composite = 0.25 * normalized_perplexity_score + 0.30 * mmlu_score + 0.20 * rouge_bleu_score + 0.15 * semantic_score + 0.10 * qa_f1_score. We will expose weights as per-project config for tuning.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Unit-tested metric implementations with edge cases (empty refs, long sequences, multi-turn contexts).
2) Calibration job produces per-profile artifacts (json metrics) for FP8 and INT8 variants for at least 3 models (llama-2-like, mixture-of-experts-lite, and a decoder-only 7B).
3) Console shows profile metric histograms and composite score; gating API returns pass/fail and explanatory deltas.
4) Canary rollout uses gating decisions to automatically prevent a profile if composite drop > configured threshold.
5) Performance: scorer computes aggregated metrics for a 10k-sample eval set in under 10 minutes on a 4-GPU calibration runner (parallelized), and memory usage stays within calibration job limits.

Risk & tradeoffs:
- Aggregation decisions can hide task-specific regressions; we will always surface task-level metrics alongside composite.
- Perplexity is sensitive to detokenization and truncation; we enforce canonical tokenization and sequence handling in the runner.
- Semantic metrics rely on a reference embedder; if the embedder drifts, thresholds must be re-calibrated.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Metric library: add a new package redwood/quant_eval/metrics with pure-Python implementations + optional Cython speedups for BLEU/ROUGE hotspots.
2) Contrast runner: a calibration subtask that runs float baseline and quant variants on identical seeds and saves per-sample outputs to s3/obj store.
3) Comparator: lightweight service that computes deltas and composite scores; exposes REST API used by calibration and Console.
4) Console: new panel and alerting rules; bind sample-failure viewer to the stored output diffs.
5) Rollout gating: implement a gate hook in the deployment manager to call comparator before profile activation.

Observability: emit per-metric histograms, N-sample burn-in reports, and a 'regression signature' artifact (top-k worst-case samples with diffs).

Documentation: add design doc in Confluence (link in attachments) and a developer quickstart for running the local contrastive scorer against a model checkpoint.

2025-11-06 - Oliver Patel: Implemented base perplexity and MMLU scoring functions. Pushed prototype to branch feat/contrastive-scorer. See PR #237. Unit tests for empty-ref cases added.
2025-11-09 - Priya Singh (PM): Requested per-project weights and an ability to override thresholds for enterprise customers. Added as scope item.
2025-11-11 - Security team (note): No customer data will be stored unmasked in the scorer; examples stored for debugging must be redacted unless opt-in. Follow-up action created for redaction helper.
2025-11-13 - QA: Found inconsistency in ROUGE between sacre-compatible implementation and our library for long summaries; added bootstrapping test and increased sample size for CI.

2025-11-15 - Oliver Patel: Performance tuning: moved BLEU tokenization to tokenized input path and introduced a streaming aggregator to reduce memory. Benchmark: 10k samples in 7m42s on 4xA100(40G) equivalent.
2025-11-18 - Maya Chen: Design review complete. Next: integrate gating API and add Console panel. Roadmap updated in Confluence doc.
notes: Keep comparator deterministic with seed-controlled sampling. Early experiments show FP8 tends to increase perplexity but has minor effect on closed-book multi-choice; thresholds should be task-specific.
